### `extract_table_schema`

```python
extract_table_schema(fully_qualified_table_name: str, *, include_metadata: bool=True, exclude_idenity_column: bool=False) -> StructType
```

Retrieve the schema structure of a Unity Catalog table.

This function requires an already-active Spark session. It reads table
metadata but does not trigger a table-data action. When identity exclusion
is requested, :func:`get_identity_column` performs additional metadata SQL.

Args:
    fully_qualified_table_name: Fully qualified table name (``catalog.schema.table``).
    include_metadata: Whether to retain column metadata such as comments. Defaults to True.
    exclude_idenity_column: Whether to remove the first detected identity
        column. The misspelling is part of the public signature.

Returns:
    ``StructType`` describing the table schema.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the table name is empty.
    Exception: Re-raises Spark, session, catalog, and identity-lookup
        failures as the same exception type with added table context.

### `find_matching_tables`

```python
find_matching_tables(catalog_name: str, schema_name: str, table_pattern: str) -> List[str]
```

Retrieve Unity Catalog tables matching a glob pattern.

The active Spark session is changed with ``USE <catalog>.<schema>`` and is
not restored. ``SHOW TABLES`` results are collected to the driver, then
matched case-insensitively with :func:`fnmatch.fnmatch` against table names.

Args:
    catalog_name: Catalog name (for example, ``"main"``).
    schema_name: Schema/database name (for example, ``"bronze"``).
    table_pattern: Case-insensitive glob pattern for table names.

Returns:
    Fully qualified matching table names in ``SHOW TABLES`` order.

Raises:
    ValueError: If any argument is empty.
    RuntimeError: If no active SparkSession exists.
    Exception: Re-raises Spark errors as the same exception type with added
        lookup context.

### `get_identity_column`

```python
get_identity_column(table_name: str) -> Optional[str]
```

Return the identity column name for a Delta table, if present.

For a three-part name, the function first queries
``system.information_schema`` and suppresses any error from that attempt.
It then parses the first identity declaration in ``SHOW CREATE TABLE``.
An active Spark session is reused or one is created.

Args:
    table_name: Fully qualified or two-part table name to inspect.

Returns:
    Identity column name if found; otherwise ``None``.

Raises:
    Exception: Propagates ``SHOW CREATE TABLE`` and Spark access failures.

### `get_partition_columns`

```python
get_partition_columns(table_name: str) -> List[str]
```

Return the list of partition column names for a table.

The function tries ``DESCRIBE DETAIL``, ``SHOW CREATE TABLE`` parsing, and
one ``SHOW PARTITIONS`` row in order. Every strategy suppresses its own
errors, so an empty result can mean either no partitions or inaccessible
metadata. An active Spark session is reused or one is created.

Args:
    table_name: Fully qualified table name to inspect.

Returns:
    List of partition column names, or an empty list when none are defined.

### `create_table`

```python
create_table(table_name: str, schema: StructType, runtime_version: str, partition_cols: Optional[List[str]]=None, identity_col: Optional[Tuple[str, int, bool]]=None, tblproperties: Optional[Dict[str, str]]=None, comment: Optional[str]=None, replace: bool=False)
```

Create or destructively replace a Delta table.

This legacy helper emits SQL from the supplied identifiers and schema.
When the table exists and ``replace`` is false, it returns without applying
schema, property, or comment changes. With ``replace=True``, ``CREATE OR
REPLACE TABLE`` replaces the existing definition and data.

The optional identity column is emitted first as non-null ``BIGINT``.
Schema field nullability is otherwise not emitted. Field comments, a table
comment, partition columns, and table properties are interpolated into the
DDL, which is logged at ``INFO``. Runtime properties use an exact preset or
fall back to the first configured preset; caller properties override them.

Args:
    table_name: Fully qualified target table name.
    schema: Spark ``StructType`` defining table columns.
    runtime_version: Databricks runtime version used to select table properties.
    partition_cols: Optional partition column names.
    identity_col: Optional tuple of column name, start value, and whether the identity
        is ``ALWAYS`` (True) or ``BY DEFAULT`` (False).
    tblproperties: Additional table properties to merge with runtime defaults.
    comment: Optional table comment.
    replace: Whether to replace an existing table.

Returns:
    None. The table is created, replaced, or left unchanged.

Raises:
    Exception: Propagates schema construction and Spark SQL failures.

Warning:
    ``replace=True`` is destructive to the existing table. Identifiers and
    table-property strings are not independently quoted or validated.

### `get_single_val_sql`

```python
get_single_val_sql(sql_query: str, *, col: Optional[str]=None, default: Any=None)
```

Return one value from the first row of a Spark SQL result.

This legacy helper performs no input validation or retries. A requested
column is matched case-insensitively using the first match. ``default`` is
returned for no rows, no result columns, or no matching column; a SQL
``NULL`` value is returned as ``None`` rather than replaced by ``default``.

Args:
    sql_query: SQL query to execute.
    col: Column name to extract (case-insensitive). If omitted, the first column is used.
    default: Value returned if no rows are found or the column is missing.

Returns:
    The value from the requested column, or ``default`` when unavailable.

Raises:
    Exception: Propagates Spark SQL and result-access errors.

### `get_min_max_records`

```python
get_min_max_records(table_path: str, filter_column: str, filter_operation: str='MAX', group_by: Optional[str]=None, additional_where_clause: Optional[str]=None) -> DataFrame
```

Retrieve records filtered by a MIN or MAX aggregation on a column.

All relation, column, grouping, and predicate strings are inserted directly
into generated Spark SQL. ``additional_where_clause`` is applied inside the
aggregation and again to the returned table alias. The query is lazy until
the returned DataFrame is acted on, and no retry is performed.

Args:
    table_path: SQL relation text for both ``FROM`` clauses.
    filter_column: SQL expression aggregated and joined to ``agg_value``.
    filter_operation: Aggregation to apply (``"MAX"`` or ``"MIN"``).
    group_by: Optional SQL grouping expression also used as one
        alias-qualified join expression.
    additional_where_clause: Optional SQL predicate applied to both query
        levels.

Returns:
    Spark ``DataFrame`` containing rows matching the aggregated value.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``filter_operation`` is not ``"MAX"`` or ``"MIN"``.
    Exception: Propagates Spark SQL analysis and execution errors.

### `batch_update`

```python
batch_update(df: DataFrame, full_table_name: str, *, mode: str='replace', batch_column: Optional[str]=None, batch_id: Optional[str]=None, evolve_schema: bool=False)
```

Destructively replace one batch or an entire Delta table.

``replace`` uses an overwrite with ``replaceWhere`` and a string equality
predicate. ``overwrite`` replaces the complete table. Writes are attempted
once with no retry. This is the legacy predecessor of
:func:`delta_batch_update`.

Args:
    df: Input Spark ``DataFrame``.
    full_table_name: Fully qualified table name (for example, ``"cat.db.tbl"``).
    mode: ``"replace"`` (replace rows matching ``batch_column``/``batch_id``) or
        ``"overwrite"`` (replace the entire table).
    batch_column: Column used in the ``replaceWhere`` predicate for replace mode.
    batch_id: String value used in the predicate when ``mode`` is
        ``"replace"``.
    evolve_schema: If True:
        - replace mode: enable ``mergeSchema`` (add new columns)
        - overwrite mode: enable ``overwriteSchema`` (table schema becomes df schema)

Returns:
    None. Matching or complete table data is overwritten.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``mode`` is invalid, ``batch_column`` is missing, or ``batch_id`` is
        missing for replace mode.
    Exception: Propagates invalid argument types and Delta write failures.

Warning:
    Both modes are destructive. The batch column is interpolated without
    identifier quoting, and this helper adds no rollback.

### `safe_write_to_delta`

```python
safe_write_to_delta(df, table_name: str, *, merge_schema: bool=False, mode: str='append', max_retry: int=5, retry_delay: float=2.0) -> None
```

Write a DataFrame to Delta with retries on transient concurrency errors.

Retryability is determined by exception-message substrings for Delta
metadata/concurrency errors and ``temporarily unavailable``. ``max_retry``
counts retries after the initial attempt, for at most
``max_retry + 1`` writes. Backoff is exponential from ``retry_delay`` plus
less than one second of random jitter.

This function does not validate retry inputs. A negative ``max_retry``
skips the loop and returns without writing; a negative calculated sleep can
raise from :func:`time.sleep`.

Args:
    df: Spark ``DataFrame`` to write.
    table_name: Fully qualified Delta table name.
    merge_schema: Whether to allow schema evolution. Defaults to False.
    mode: Write mode (for example, ``"append"`` or ``"overwrite"``). Defaults to ``"append"``.
    max_retry: Number of retries after the initial attempt.
    retry_delay: Base delay in seconds for exponential backoff.

Returns:
    None. Data is written as a side effect.

Raises:
    Exception: Propagates non-retryable failures, the last exhausted
        retryable failure, and invalid sleep values.

Warning:
    The selected Spark write mode may be destructive. Retrying a write can
    repeat external side effects; no idempotency check is added.

### `safe_run_sql`

```python
safe_run_sql(query: str, *, max_retry: int=5, retry_delay: float=2.0) -> DataFrame
```

Execute a SQL query with automatic retry handling.

Retryability and exponential backoff match :func:`safe_write_to_delta`.
``max_retry`` counts retries after the initial call. Because Spark SQL is
lazy for many statements, only errors raised by ``spark.sql(query)`` itself
are retried; failures from later actions on the returned DataFrame are not.

Args:
    query: SQL query to execute.
    max_retry: Number of retries after the initial call.
    retry_delay: Base delay in seconds for exponential backoff.

Returns:
    Spark ``DataFrame`` containing the query result.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``max_retry`` or ``retry_delay`` is negative.
    Exception: Propagates Spark errors when retries are exhausted or errors are non-retryable.

Warning:
    ``query`` may be mutating. Retrying it can repeat external side effects,
    and this helper performs no idempotency check.

### `delta_batch_update`

```python
delta_batch_update(df: DataFrame, full_table_name: str, *, mode: str='replace', batch_column: Optional[str]=None, batch_id: Optional[Union[str, int, date]]=None, evolve_schema: bool=False) -> None
```

Append a DataFrame or replace part or all of a Delta table.

In ``append`` mode, every DataFrame row is added and the batch arguments
must be omitted. In ``replace`` mode, rows matching
``batch_column = batch_id`` are atomically replaced through Delta Lake's
``replaceWhere`` option. An empty DataFrame is valid in ``replace`` mode
and can therefore remove the matching rows without inserting replacements.

Args:
    df: DataFrame to write.
    full_table_name: Fully qualified target table name.
    mode: ``"append"`` to add rows, ``"replace"`` for one batch, or
        ``"overwrite"`` for the complete table. The value is
        case-insensitive.
    batch_column: Column identifying the batch in ``replace`` mode. Must
        be omitted in ``append`` mode.
    batch_id: Batch value. Supported values are strings, integers, and
        dates, subject to the Spark type of ``batch_column``. Must be
        omitted in ``append`` mode.
    evolve_schema: Enable schema merging for append or batch replacement,
        or schema overwrite for complete-table replacement.

Returns:
    None. A Delta write is committed as a side effect.

Raises:
    TypeError: If an argument type is incompatible with the corresponding
        Spark type, or if the batch-column Spark type is unsupported.
    ValueError: If the mode or required replacement arguments are invalid.
    Exception: Propagates Delta and Spark write failures. No retry is
        performed.

Warning:
    ``replace`` destructively removes the matching batch before inserting
    the supplied rows; an empty DataFrame can therefore delete that batch.
    ``overwrite`` destructively replaces the complete table.

### `delta_merge`

```python
delta_merge(source_df: DataFrame, full_table_name: str, join_keys: Sequence[str], *, update_columns: Optional[Sequence[str]]=None, insert_columns: Optional[Sequence[str]]=None, matched_condition: Optional[Column]=None) -> None
```

Merge a source DataFrame into an existing Delta table.

Source and target rows are matched with null-safe equality on every join
key. By default, matched rows update every source column except join keys
and the target identity column, while unmatched rows insert every source
column except the identity column. Pass an empty sequence for
``update_columns`` or ``insert_columns`` to disable that merge clause.

The target schema is read at call time. Schema evolution is not enabled,
identity columns cannot be written, and Delta/Spark validates source and
target data-type compatibility when the merge executes. This function
performs one merge attempt and deliberately does not retry failures.

The caller must ensure that at most one source row matches each target row;
otherwise Delta can reject the merge as ambiguous.

Args:
    source_df: DataFrame containing rows to update or insert.
    full_table_name: Fully qualified name of an existing Delta table.
    join_keys: One or more columns used to match source and target rows.
    update_columns: Columns copied from the source for matched rows.
        Defaults to all source columns except join keys and the identity
        column. An empty sequence disables matched-row updates.
    insert_columns: Columns copied from the source for unmatched rows.
        Defaults to all source columns except the identity column. An empty
        sequence disables unmatched-row inserts.
    matched_condition: Optional PySpark ``Column`` predicate limiting
        matched-row updates. Build alias-qualified predicates with the
        aliases ``source`` and ``target``.

Returns:
    None. The Delta merge is committed as a side effect.

Raises:
    TypeError: If a column collection or ``matched_condition`` has an
        invalid type.
    ValueError: If the table name, column collections, source schema, or
        requested merge clauses are invalid, or the target table does not
        exist.
    Exception: Propagates Spark and Delta errors without retrying.

Warning:
    This function mutates the target table by updating matched rows and/or
    inserting unmatched rows.

### `delta_insert`

```python
delta_insert(full_table_name: str, values: Union[Mapping[str, Any], Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]]) -> None
```

Append one or more Python mappings to an existing Delta table.

The target schema is loaded at call time with :func:`extract_table_schema`.
Each mapping may omit nullable columns; omitted nullable columns are written
as SQL ``NULL``. Non-nullable columns must be present, although values that
are explicitly supplied as ``None`` are left for PySpark and Delta Lake to
validate. Any identity column is removed from both the DataFrame schema and
the input rows so Databricks can generate its value. Other unknown columns
are rejected, and the caller's mappings are never mutated.

Args:
    full_table_name: Name of an existing Delta table, typically qualified as
        ``catalog.schema.table``.
    values: One row as a mapping of column names to Python values, or a
        non-empty sequence of such mappings.

Returns:
    None. Rows are appended to ``full_table_name`` as a side effect.

Raises:
    TypeError: If ``values`` is not a mapping or sequence of mappings.
    ValueError: If the table name is empty, the table does not exist, no
        rows are provided, a row contains unknown columns, or a row omits
        a non-nullable column.
    Exception: Propagates schema-resolution, DataFrame-creation, and Delta
        write errors with their original traceback.

Note:
    A missing nullable column is materialized as ``NULL`` and therefore
    does not invoke a default expression defined on that table column.

Warning:
    This function mutates the target table by appending rows.

### `delta_delete`

```python
delta_delete(full_table_name: str, key_values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None
```

Delete rows from an existing Delta table by exact key values.

All entries in ``key_values`` are combined with logical ``AND``. Values are
validated against their target ``StructField`` definitions by constructing
a temporary one-row DataFrame with the selected table schema. The temporary
DataFrame is not persisted. A Python ``None`` value matches SQL ``NULL``;
other values are represented as typed Spark literals. An empty mapping is
rejected to prevent an accidental full-table deletion.

Args:
    full_table_name: Name of an existing Delta table, typically qualified as
        ``catalog.schema.table``.
    key_values: Non-empty mapping of target column names to exact values.

Returns:
    None. Matching rows are deleted as a Delta transaction. No matching rows
    is considered a successful operation.

Raises:
    TypeError: If ``key_values`` is not a mapping, a key is not a string, or
        PySpark rejects a value for its target data type.
    ValueError: If the table name or mapping is empty, the table does not
        exist, a key is empty or unknown, or PySpark rejects a value because
        of nullability or range constraints.
    Exception: Propagates schema-resolution and Delta transaction errors
        with their original traceback.

Warning:
    Row deletion is destructive. Every target row matching all key values
    is removed, with no recovery or confirmation step.

### `delta_update`

```python
delta_update(full_table_name: str, key_values: Mapping[str, Any], values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None
```

Update rows in an existing Delta table by exact key values.

All entries in ``key_values`` are combined with logical ``AND``. Only the
columns present in ``values`` are updated; all other columns remain
unchanged. Keys and replacement values are validated independently against
their target ``StructField`` definitions by constructing temporary one-row
DataFrames. The temporary DataFrames are not persisted. Python ``None``
matches SQL ``NULL`` in a key and assigns SQL ``NULL`` in an update when the
corresponding column is nullable.

Args:
    full_table_name: Name of an existing Delta table, typically qualified as
        ``catalog.schema.table``.
    key_values: Non-empty mapping of target column names to exact values
        used to select rows.
    values: Non-empty mapping of target column names to replacement values.

Returns:
    None. Matching rows are updated as a Delta transaction. No matching rows
    is considered a successful operation.

Raises:
    TypeError: If ``key_values`` or ``values`` is not a mapping, a column
        name is not a string, or PySpark rejects a value for its target data
        type.
    ValueError: If the table name or either mapping is empty, the table does
        not exist, a column name is empty or unknown, an identity column is
        included in ``values``, or PySpark rejects a value because of
        nullability or range constraints.
    Exception: Propagates schema-resolution and Delta transaction errors
        with their original traceback.

Warning:
    This function destructively replaces the selected column values for
    every row matching all key values.

### `delta_execute_sql`

```python
delta_execute_sql(sql_query: str) -> DataFrame
```

Execute a SQL statement and return its Spark DataFrame result.

The function performs no automatic retries because ``sql_query`` may be a
mutating statement that is unsafe to repeat. Spark SQL supports Delta and
non-Delta statements; the ``delta`` prefix groups this function with the
other table utilities in this module.

Args:
    sql_query: Non-empty SQL statement to execute.

Returns:
    Spark ``DataFrame`` representing the statement result.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``sql_query`` is not a non-empty string.
    Exception: Propagates Spark SQL analysis and execution errors with their
        original traceback.

### `delta_fetch_scalar`

```python
delta_fetch_scalar(sql_query: str, *, column: Optional[str]=None, default: Any=None) -> Any
```

Return one value from the first row of a SQL result.

If ``column`` is omitted, the first result column is selected. ``default``
is returned only when the query produces no rows. A SQL ``NULL`` cell is
returned as Python ``None``, and an invalid column name raises an exception.

Args:
    sql_query: Non-empty SQL query to execute.
    column: Optional result-column name. Matching prefers an exact name and
        then allows one unambiguous case-insensitive match.
    default: Value returned when the result contains no rows.

Returns:
    The selected value from the first row, or ``default`` for no rows.

Raises:
    TypeError: If ``column`` is neither a string nor ``None``.
    ValueError: If the query is empty or the result column cannot be
        resolved unambiguously.
    Exception: Propagates Spark SQL errors with their original traceback.

### `delta_fetch_column`

```python
delta_fetch_column(sql_query: str, *, column: Optional[str]=None) -> List[Any]
```

Return all values from one column of a SQL result.

The selected column is streamed to the driver with ``toLocalIterator`` to
avoid materializing the entire result at once. The returned list still grows
with the result size, so callers should keep queries appropriately bounded.

Args:
    sql_query: Non-empty SQL query to execute.
    column: Optional result-column name. Matching prefers an exact name and
        then allows one unambiguous case-insensitive match.

Returns:
    List containing every selected value, including Python ``None`` for SQL
    ``NULL``. Returns an empty list when the query produces no rows.

Raises:
    TypeError: If ``column`` is neither a string nor ``None``.
    ValueError: If the query is empty or the result column cannot be
        resolved unambiguously.
    Exception: Propagates Spark SQL errors with their original traceback.
